title: Normalized runtime overlay (GET /nexus/health)
description: UNLIKE every other schema in this tree, this one describes an API RESPONSE rather than an authored artifact: the one normalized operational document Nexus and the CLI both consume (design 12, design 15). It is never written to Git and never hand-edited. Every operational source - Argo CD, Grafana alerts, uptime, evals, backups, communication, server reconciliation - reports through one Source shape carrying its own adapter status and observation time, so a source that is unconfigured or failed reads unknown instead of disappearing into green. The rollup ladder (unhealthy > degraded > unknown > healthy) is applied HERE, at the producer, and nowhere else: browser and CLI read levels, they never compute them. v1alpha2 (#565/#567): the rollup key space gains the `bundle:<name>` scope (per canonical installed Bundle) and `bucket:unbundled` (agents outside every bundle).

level.description: The severity ladder. `unknown` is NOT a synonym for healthy: it is what a source reports when it has no observation, and it outranks healthy in every rollup.

sourceKind.description: Closed set. Adding a kind is a new schema version directory, never a silent widening - consumers switch on this exhaustively.

adapterStatus.description: `stale` IS the last-good marker: the current collection failed and what you see is the previous observation, whose age is the difference between this source's observedAt and the document's. `failed` means it failed with no last-good to fall back on. Both must carry level `unknown` or the previous level - never a fresh green.

link.description: Server-built and server-sanitized. `url` is an absolute allowlisted http(s) destination assembled from exact identity (an Argo Application's namespace AND name, never a card title); `href` is an in-Nexus route, safe by construction. Exactly one of the two.

observedAt.description: When the DATA was observed, not when this response was built. Older than the document's observedAt exactly when the source is stale.

reasons.description: Bounded so a hostile upstream message cannot blow a popover open. A truncated list ends with a `+N more` reason.

rollup.description: A precomputed aggregate over a named set. `members` lists the AFFECTED component ids (degraded or unhealthy), sorted - which is what turns 'follow the red dot down' into a lookup rather than a second calculation in the browser.

observedAt.description: When this document was built. Per-source observedAt may be older.

stale.description: True when any source is serving last-good data. Drives the UI's stale banner, so the banner is a server fact rather than a browser inference from a failed poll.

sources.description: Every source kind, always present. A kind with no data path says so through its status; it is never omitted, because an omitted row is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

components.description: Workload components only (agents and applications). People and Groups carry no health and are absent by design.

sources.description: One entry per source kind, narrowed to this component. Present even when every adapter is unconfigured - the browser renders these rows verbatim and must never fabricate one.

rollups.description: Precomputed aggregates, keyed `<scope>:<name>`. `kind:agent` and `kind:application` are the directory rollups; `group:<id>` mirrors the canvas containment fields, computed over ALL members including collapsed ones; `bucket:ungrouped` covers the workload components no group claims (a separate scope so it can never collide with a real group whose id happens to be `ungrouped`). Later milestones register `sheet:<id>` and `nav:<surface>` here - the key space is deliberately open so a new surface needs no schema version. v1alpha2 adds `bundle:<name>` (canonical installed Bundle membership, #567) and `bucket:unbundled`.

integrations.description: Legacy summary booleans. Superseded by `sources[].status`; retained so an older browser bundle keeps rendering.
